chunks: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Marwazi narrated to us from his father, from Yahya ibn Abbas, from Ali ibn Amir al-Wasiti, who said: I was informed by Ata ibn al-Sayb, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Amir, who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: While his companions were recalling the virtues of the month of Shaban in his presence,

He said: It is a noble month, and it is my month. The Throne bears it, honors it, and recognizes its right. It is a month in which Allah increases the sustenance of the believers for Ramadan, and in which the gardens (of Paradise) are adorned.
It is named Shaban because the sustenance of the believers branches out for Ramadan within it.

It is the month of deeds. In it, good deeds are multiplied seventyfold, evil deeds are erased, sins are forgiven, and good deeds are accepted. The Almighty (Glorified is His Majesty) boasts in it with His servants, looking from His Throne to His fasting and praying servants, and boasting of them to the bearers of His Throne.

Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) stood up and said: My father and mother be sacrificed for you, O Messenger of Allah. Describe to us something of its virtue so that we may increase our desire for its fasting and night prayer, and perform Tahajjud for the Majestic One in it.
He (peace be upon him) said: Whoever fasts the first day of Shaban, Allah writes for him seventy good deeds, and each good deed is equivalent to the worship of a year.
And whoever fasts two days of Shaban, He removes from him the destructive evil deed.
And whoever fasts three days of Shaban, He raises him seventy degrees in the Gardens (of Paradise) made of pearls and rubies.
And whoever fasts four days of Shaban, He expands his sustenance.
And whoever fasts five days of Shaban, he becomes beloved to the servants.
And whoever fasts six days of Shaban, Allah turns away from him seventy types of calamities.
And whoever fasts seven days of Shaban, he is protected from Satan and his troops, from his nudging and whispering.
And whoever fasts eight days of Shaban, he will not leave this world until he is given a drink from the cisterns of Holiness.
And whoever fasts nine days of Shaban, Munkar and Nakir are lenient with him when they question him.
And whoever fasts ten days of Shaban, Allah expands his grave seventy cubits by seventy cubits.
And whoever fasts eleven days, Allah sets up eleven minarets of light over his grave.
And whoever fasts twelve days of Shaban, seventy thousand thousand angels visit him in his grave every day until the blowing of the Trumpet.
And whoever fasts thirteen days of Shaban, the angels of the seven heavens seek forgiveness for him.
And whoever fasts fourteen days of Shaban, beasts and wild animals, even fish in the seas, are inspired to seek forgiveness for him.
And whoever fasts fifteen days of Shaban, the Lord of Glory calls out to him: 'By My Honor, I will not burn you in the Fire.'
And whoever fasts sixteen days of Shaban, He extinguishes for him seventy seas of Hellfire, all of them.
And whoever fasts seventeen days of Shaban, all the doors of Hell are closed for him.
And whoever fasts eighteen days of Shaban, all the doors of the Gardens are opened for him.
And whoever fasts nineteen days of Shaban, he is given seventy thousand palaces in the Gardens made of pearls and rubies.
And whoever fasts twenty days of Shaban, he is married to seventy thousand Hur al-Ayn.
And whoever fasts twenty-one days of Shaban, the angels become obligated to him and brush him with their wings.
And whoever fasts twenty-two days of Shaban, he is clothed in seventy thousand garments of silk and brocade.
And whoever fasts twenty-three days of Shaban, a mount of light is brought to him when he exits his grave, and he rides it flying to Paradise.
And whoever fasts twenty-four days of Shaban, he intercedes for seventy thousand people of monotheism.
And whoever fasts twenty-five days of Shaban, he is given a certificate of freedom from hypocrisy.
And whoever fasts twenty-six days of Shaban, Allah writes for him a permit across the Sirat (Bridge).
And whoever fasts twenty-seven days of Shaban, Allah writes for him a certificate of freedom from the Fire.
And whoever fasts twenty-eight days of Shaban, his face becomes radiant.
And whoever fasts twenty-nine days of Shaban, he attains the greatest pleasure of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

And whoever fasts thirty days of Shaban, Jibreel (peace be upon him) calls out to him from before the Throne: 'O this one! Begin anew with a new deed, for what has passed and what preceded of your sins have been forgiven.'

And the Majestic One, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'If your sins were the number of the stars of the sky, the drops of rain, the leaves of trees, the count of sand and dust, and the days of the world, I would forgive them for you.'
And that is not difficult for Allah after your fasting of the month of Shaban.
Ibn Abbas said: This is for the month of Shaban.

key_terms.الصِّرَاط: The Bridge over Hellfire on the Day of Judgment
key_terms.سَبْعِينَ: Seventy, often used to denote a large multiplication of reward
key_terms.شَهْرُ شَعْبَانَ: The month of Shaban, the eighth month of the Islamic lunar calendar
key_terms.مُنْكَرٌ وَ نَكِيرٌ: The two angels who question the deceased in the grave

ai.seo_question: What are the specific rewards for fasting each day of the month of Shaban according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Compiled by Shaykh al-Saduq, this hadith emphasizes Shaban as the 'month of preparation' (Shahr al-Ziyadah) where sustenance is distributed for Ramadan, a concept deeply rooted in Shia devotional practice. It details specific rewards for fasting each day, culminating in a comprehensive forgiveness of sins, with the Prophet (saw) noting that God boasts to the Bearers of the Throne about its fasting servants, reinforcing its status as a precursor to the holy month.
